title: Sorting after Repartitioning PySpark Dataframe
question:
We have a giant file which we repartitioned according to one column, for example, say it is STATE. Now it seems like after repartitioning, the data cannot be sorted completely. We are trying to save our final file as a text file but instead of the first state listed being Alabama, now California shows up first. OrderBy doesn't seem to have an effect after running the repartition.

df = df.repartition(100, ['STATE_NAME'])\
    .sortWithinPartitions('STATE_NAME', 'CUSTOMER_ID', 'ROW_ID')
answer:
It is first important to clarify the difference between various sorting operations available in pyspark.

.sort() .orderBy() are aliases for the same operation and both perform global ordering of data (across the entire table)

.sortWithinPartitions() sorts data within each partition of the table, independently.

https://stackoverflow.com/a/66535831/12609881

repartition() can trigger a shuffle and compromise any prior global ordering or local ordering of the table.

It is not clear exactly what you are trying to accomplish since the sample code you provided contradicts the global ordering you appear to desire. If you need global ordering AND are particular about partition count / size, you will require workarounds as described in this forum: https://www.reddit.com/r/apachespark/comments/sxerdh/repartition_maintaining_sort/

The issue is when I load a df, sort and then partition, it is losing sort order on the repartition. If I repartition and then sort, it is the correct sort order but the partition count is not maintained.

since coalesce() does not trigger a shuffle it may be safer to use in your use case to preserve ordering of data and specify partition count. However, you may end up with lumpy partitions.
